newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 20.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Despite pessimistic expectations from domestic and foreign economists, GDP in the first quarter of this year showed positive growth. According to the Czech Statistical Bureau, real GDP growth was 1.5 percent. An increase in productivity was noted in trade, money and insurance, but a decrease in construction, mining and energy industries.

- In line with a cabinet proposal, Parliament Chairman Milos Zeman announced a state of legislative emergency from June 19 until July 2. This will help the cabinet, while waiting for changes in budget regulations.
- The Finance Ministry and the Industry and Trade Ministry propose gas prices should increase twice this year, once on July 1 by 15 percent and a second time, by 19 percent, in October.

- The year-on-year increase in M2 money supply in April, after subtracting deposits of SPT Telecom, amounted to 6.2 percent, compared to 7.3 percent in March. With SPT's deposits, it was 5.3 percent, compared to 6.3 percent in March.
- Shareholders of Union Banka decided yesterday to increase basic capital from 1.34 billion to 1.94 billion crowns.
- The general director of Pension Fund Jistota announced yesterday that it will merge with Rentia pension fund.
- Skoda Plzen has prepared a solution for financial restructuring of Tatra Koprivnice, which it does not want to announce. It does not rule out making Tatra bankrupt.
- Lachema Brno a.s., a leading domestic manufacturer of drugs, wants to establish a subsidiary in Germany called Adapharm s.r.o. this year.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Representatives of NATO countries will meet in Prague from today with leaders of the countries aspiring for membership. Presidents Vaclav Havel, Polish Alexander Kwasniewski and Romanian Emil Constantinescu will participate in the meeting, along with U.S. Deputy Secretary of Defence John White and NATO General George Joulwan.
- The Finance Ministry estimates that the 1998 budget will be around 560 billion crowns, and it will have a surplus of 10 billion crowns.
- Komercni Banka is decreasing its interest rates today for short-term accounts by between three and four percent. Konsolidacni Banka is decreasing its target rate by four percent.

- Privatisation of the largest domestic metal company, Nova Hut, will probably slow down, because Komercni Banka and Credit Suisse First Boston, authorised for the sale of the state's 18-percent stake, recommend postponement.

- Komercni Banka obtained a five-year credit of 250 million marks, more than 4.5 billion crowns, from a group of banks led by BZW, Dresdner Bank Luxembourg, Sanwa Bank and Union Bank of Switzerland. IPB bank also obtained a three-year loan from Dresdner Bank of $20 million, 650 million crowns.
- Bohemia Sekt will pay dividends of 100 crowns per share, 30 percent of its net profits.
- Shareholders of Moravia Banka approved an increase in basic capital of 200 million crowns yesterday, which will bring the bank's capital up to one billion crowns.
- Minority shareholders of Karosa, whose majority is owned by French Renault, did not succeed with a proposal to change shares to the owners to enable free trading.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After his first meeting with the leaders of both chambers of parliament, President Vaclav Havel said that if the current cabinet collapsed, he would meet with the current coalition to decide who would be the new prime minister and who would be trusted to form a new cabinet.
- The Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) propose new social laws be effective only until the end of 1998.

- The cabinet wants to prevent any kind of protests from disturbing construction of the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant. This is in reaction to plans for the Temelin blockade, which would take place from July 6 to 13 and have the participation of the world's most radical protestors of nuclear energy.

PRAVO - At a general meeting yesterday, shareholders of Radegast brewery approved dividends of 63.545 million crowns, 80 crowns per share, from net profits of 140 million crowns and record output of 1.921 million hectolitres of beer. The president of the brewery, Jan Sikora, denied information that British Bass obtained a majority stake.
- The Industry and Trade Ministry, representing 70 percent in a general meeting yesterday, prevented CEZ from paying dividends which would have been 22 crowns for each 1,100-crown share.
- The parliament agricultural committee for the second time went through the cabinet's proposal for an agricultural law and recommended it for the July parliament meeting.

- According to a digest for 1997 from WoodCommerz, the crown will decline by the end of the year to about 34 to the dollar and 20.50 to 21 to the mark, and the crown was overvalued by 15 to 20 percent at its former central parity.
- The cabinet should decide on the privatisation of Ceske Radiokommunikace this year.
- According to a civic law approved by the cabinet on Wednesday evening, in the future, owners of flats will be able to terminate their contract with lessors without the approval of a court.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
